newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia pledges to continue economic reforms.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia pledges to continue economic reforms.

text.p: Indonesia's senior cabinet minister said on Tuesday the government would continue reforms to liberalise the economy.
"To cope with the challenges, the Indonesian government is committed to continue its reforms," the Coordinating Minister for Production and Distribution, Hartarto, told a petrochemical conference.

He said liberalisation measures so far had "to some extent already exceeded" the country's commitments under the Uruguay Round of world trade negotiations under the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade.
"In compliance with the country's commitments in the Uruguay Round agreement, the country will further cut tariffs and non-tariff barriers," he said.
Hartarto said the government would take the necessary steps to encourage the private sector to invest in infrastructure projects.
"The government will take the necessary steps that will make investment in this sector attractive," he said.
He said the amount of funds needed to develop Indonesia's infrastructure was huge and the government realised its resources alone were insufficient.
"Therefore, the government will encourage the participation of the private sector in the development of infrastructure," he said.
Hartarto said Indonesia was confident the exports would strengthen.

"Last year the government released policy packages that besides being directed at increasing efficiency were also intended to push exports. In the coming years the policies should bear fruit," he said.
Indonesia posted a trade surplus of $6.98 billion in 1996/97 against $5.18 billion in 1995/96.
